CSL. Always Evolving for a Better World.

CSL has delivered biotechnology excellence for over a century. Today, with the combined expertise of CSL Behring, CSL Plasma, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor, CSL’s offerings are more diverse than ever to help ensure patients and people everywhere get the treatments they need. We’re always improving so life can, too.

Protecting public health and communities from seasonal influenza is at the heart of what CSL’s vaccines business, CSL Seqirus, does. This commitment was recently highlighted when Jim Sherner, Executive Director and Head of Policy, Advocacy, and Government Affairs at CSL Seqirus, shared insights at a National Adult and Influenza Immunization Summit \(NAIIS\) panel about influenza vaccination challenges for this upcoming year and the importance of receiving annual vaccination against seasonal influenza. Pictured below on day one of trading in 1994: CSL’s General Manager, Finance and Planning, Graeme Kaufman; Company Secretary, Peter Tuohy; Managing Director \(and current Chair\), Dr Brian McNamee; Company Chairman, Colin Harper; and Manager, Companies at the Melbourne Stock Exchange, Alan Shaw.

30 May

Together with a small group of Philadelphia’s business leaders and industry stakeholders, CSL was invited to attend a reception with Pennsylvania’s Governor, Josh Shapiro and Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. Attendees heard of the strong economic ties between Canada and Pennsylvania, and more specifically, an emphasis to strengthen well established partnerships between the two trade partners and lean into future industry together. Perdita Cheshire, Director and Head of Research Innovation North America represented CSL at the event. “Fostering strategic relationships within the Canadian life sciences ecosystem remains a top priority for CSL’s North American Research Innovation Team as we build on the successful partnerships we’ve already established in the US. This event reinforced the importance of collaboration and innovation in order to improve the lives of patients worldwide,” said Dr Cheshire.
